candidates.name: nycdb
candidates.what_it_holds: Python program that downloads, processes, and loads 40+ NYC public housing/property datasets into a single PostgreSQL database in one command: PLUTO (parcel-level land use, ~857k lots), DOB job filings/complaints/violations/vacate orders/certificates of occupancy, HPD violations/registrations/litigations/complaints, DOF Rolling Sales and Tax Lien Sales, ACRIS (deeds and mortgage documents), Evictions, ECB Violations, Property Address Directory, rodent inspections, subsidized-housing database, corporate/ownership records. 796 commits, code AGPLv3, prebuilt database files CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
candidates.why_useful: Directly fills gap 13 (long-term rental/housing supply economics) and touches NYC PLUTO/ACRIS specifically named in the theme; a one-command ingest of parcel, permit, ownership, sales and rent-registration data for the largest ABNB metro, letting the team build NYC host-supply/LTR-STR crossover series without hand-scraping NYC Open Data endpoints one by one.
candidates.time_coverage: varies by dataset, generally 2000s-present, updated periodically
candidates.license: Code AGPLv3; loaded data CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial)
candidates.last_activity: active, exact date not surfaced by fetch
candidates.size_hint: 40+ source tables, city-wide (largest tables ~millions of rows, e.g. DOB complaints, HPD violations)

candidates.name: who-owns-what (JustFix.nyc)
candidates.what_it_holds: Django/PostgreSQL + React app and backend SQL functions that map NYC landlord portfolios and shell-company/LLC ownership networks using HPD Registration (~160k properties), PLUTO, and ACRIS deed/ownership records; identifies buildings a given owner network controls and flags financially distressed buildings. 1,172 commits, GPLv3, ~39 open issues, ongoing maintenance.
candidates.why_useful: Purpose-built LLC-ownership-network tool over NYC PLUTO/ACRIS/HPD data -- exactly the 'LLC ownership' and 'NYC PLUTO/ACRIS' items named in the theme; usable to identify institutional/investor-controlled rental portfolios in NYC as a host-supply-concentration proxy (gap 13).
candidates.time_coverage: HPD registrations current + historical filings, ongoing

candidates.name: hmda-platform (CFPB)
candidates.what_it_holds: CFPB's official regulatory-technology platform for Home Mortgage Disclosure Act (HMDA) filings: parses/validates pipe-delimited Transmission (TS) and Loan Application Register (LAR) files, and exposes filing APIs, a data browser, analytics dashboards and a rate-spread calculator with documented REST endpoints for pulling loan-level mortgage origination data (loan amount, rate spread, applicant/property geography, action taken) nationwide. 11,916 commits, CC0-1.0 (public domain).
candidates.why_useful: Provides a maintained, documented method to pull nationwide loan-level mortgage rate/origination data by county/tract and year -- directly useful for a mortgage-rate and housing-finance-conditions series feeding the host-supply-economics work in gap 13; CC0 licensing removes any reuse friction.
candidates.time_coverage: current HMDA reporting years (platform), historical LAR data available via CFPB HMDA data browser going back to ~2007
candidates.last_activity: actively maintained (58 open issues, 5 open PRs)
candidates.size_hint: national loan-level LAR files, tens of millions of records/year

candidates.name: mcp-atlas
candidates.what_it_holds: MCP server (npm package @urbankitstudio/mcp-atlas) providing a uniform query interface over ~137-155 US county parcel ArcGIS REST endpoints; tools for owner/taxpayer name lookup (case-insensitive partial match, useful for identifying LLC-named owners), APN lookup, and site/mailing address retrieval. MIT license, 13 commits, 2026 copyright.
candidates.why_useful: A ready-made client for pulling county assessor/parcel-owner records (including LLC-style owner names) across a large multi-state county set without hand-building per-county ArcGIS queries -- directly on-theme for 'county assessor/parcel data' and 'LLC ownership'.
candidates.time_coverage: current parcel-roll snapshot (live query, not historical)
candidates.size_hint: 13 commits, thin wrapper -- no committed dataset, live API pass-through

candidates.name: openaddresses
candidates.what_it_holds: Global collection (14,515+ commits) of source manifests (CC0 JSON metadata) for address, cadastral parcel, building footprint and street-centerline datasets, with a `us-data/` tree covering many US counties/states; processed outputs downloadable from openaddresses.io. Source metadata CC0-1.0; repo code BSD-3; underlying data retains original licenses.
candidates.why_useful: A discovery/aggregation layer over hundreds of county and municipal parcel/cadastral data sources (many of which include building footprints and, indirectly, parcel counts usable as a housing-stock/permit-adjacent proxy) -- fills the 'county assessor/parcel data' item at national/international scale rather than one county at a time.
candidates.time_coverage: snapshot of current source data, updated periodically since project inception (~2014)
candidates.license: CC0-1.0 (source metadata); BSD-3 (code); original licenses for underlying data

candidates.name: GitHub topic: building-permits (index page, not a single repo)
candidates.what_it_holds: Index of 18 repos tagged building-permits, notably: OpenPermitFees (machine-readable US building-permit fee schedules with sourcing), Shovels API client/profile repos (claims 130M+ building permits across 1,800+ US jurisdictions, 2.3M+ contractor profiles -- paid API, not a free dataset), a Vancouver building-permits Dash exploration tool, a San Diego renovation-permit analytics repo, and a BuildData Canadian construction/real-estate API sample.
candidates.why_useful: Surfaces the closest thing to a national building-permit aggregator on GitHub (Shovels), and machine-readable permit-fee schedules (OpenPermitFees) that proxy local construction-cost/regulatory friction feeding into new STR/LTR unit supply -- worth flagging even though most are thin wrappers over paid APIs.
candidates.geography: primarily US, city/county level; one Canadian, one Vancouver-specific
candidates.time_coverage: varies; Shovels claims broad historical jurisdiction coverage (unverified, paid API)
candidates.last_activity: mixed, several recent (2026) per description tone
candidates.size_hint: Shovels claims 130M+ permit records nationally (behind paid API, not verified directly)

candidates.name: HomeHarvest
candidates.what_it_holds: Python library (MIT, 739 stars, 288 commits) that scrapes Realtor.com (not actually Zillow/Redfin despite topic tagging) for MLS-style listing data: address, MLS ID, listing status, beds/baths/sqft, list/sold price, price-per-sqft, HOA fees, list/sold/last-update dates, coordinates, county, nearby schools, agent/broker info, tax history and assessment values. Outputs to CSV/Excel/Pandas/JSON.
candidates.why_useful: A maintained, no-API-key scraper for current/historical-by-repeated-pull residential listing and sold-price data at the county level, usable to build a for-sale housing supply/price series as an LTR<->STR crossover input; no dedicated investor-purchase field but sold-price + tax-assessment history could support an investor-activity proxy (repeat-buyer / fast-flip detection) if pulled longitudinally.
candidates.time_coverage: live/current listings and recent solds only, no historical archive committed

candidates.name: GitHub topic: parcel-data (index page)
candidates.what_it_holds: Index of 7 repos: CityOfDetroit/rental_map (registered-rental-property map for Detroit, Leaflet/ESRI), joshvern/citylens-web (NYC parcel intelligence + aerial/3D site analysis), Center-for-Land-Economics/civicmapper (land-value/improvement maps across 35+ cities, Python), property-boundary/property-boundary (PostGIS/GeoPandas cadastral ETL pipeline framework), pdiegel/NC-Parcel-Search (North Carolina parcel search webapp).
candidates.why_useful: CityOfDetroit/rental_map is a committed, city-published registered-rental-property dataset (STR/LTR host-supply proxy for a mid-size US market outside our current 13-city Inside Airbnb panel); civicmapper aggregates land-value data across 35+ cities and could be a cross-check for county assessor coverage.
candidates.size_hint: Detroit rental registry: city-wide; civicmapper: 35+ cities

candidates.name: GitHub topic: hmda (index page)
candidates.what_it_holds: Index of HMDA-related repos, notably a described 'hmda_database' project (harmonized DuckDB build of 40+ years of HMDA mortgage data, 685M rows, one-command build) plus several fair-lending/disparity analysis repos (hmda-racial-disparities, CATE-HMDA-Heterogeneous-Effects, hmda-analyzer, fair-lending-screener, fairlens) built on public HMDA loan-level data.
candidates.why_useful: If the 'hmda_database' project (or an equivalent) is real and reproducible, a 685M-row, 40-year harmonized mortgage-origination panel in DuckDB would be a very strong national mortgage-rate/lending-volume time series for the housing-supply-economics gap; flagged as unverified since a direct repo fetch under the described owner/name 404'd and the exact URL could not be confirmed within budget.
candidates.geography: United States, national with geographic (state/county/tract) breakdowns
candidates.time_coverage: described as 40+ years (roughly 1980s/1990s-present, matching HMDA history)
candidates.license: unverified (HMDA source data is public domain)
candidates.size_hint: 685M rows (as described in topic listing; not independently confirmed)
